subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core own a branded Agentic OS v1 lease-and-session RPC contract, or should core expose only a generic leased-spawn seam for an external owner to build on?
rationale: The current patch adds product-specific method names, metadata rules, and durable state to core. Choosing between a generic core capability and an external-owner implementation is a lasting API and ownership decision that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Define a generic core seam
options.body: Keep only reusable lease-authorized spawn primitives in core, move Agentic OS naming and orchestration policy to its owner surface, and add upgrade-safe persistence.

options.title: Approve the branded core contract
options.body: Explicitly accept Agentic OS as a core Gateway API, then require the same upgrade-safe schema path, contract documentation, and current-head proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the contract downstream
options.body: Close or replace this core PR if the existing plugin or external integration seams can own the contract without new core APIs.

recommendation.title: Define a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Keep only reusable lease-authorized spawn primitives in core, move Agentic OS naming and orchestration policy to its owner surface, and add upgrade-safe persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable person-level current-main provenance was available in the supplied review context; Gateway and state-code ownership should be selected by the repository's actual recent area owners.
